label: GO step, choosing a2 after a rewarded common trial, late in the episode (trials ~45-95)
explanation: Fires only at GO, never at D1/D2. It needs all of these: the previous trial was rewarded (no activity when prev_reward=0), the agent is about to choose a2 (model_act==2; 90% of mass is in the most negative choice-logit bin; it essentially never fires for a1), and the step is late in the episode (none before trial 40, most at 50-89, falling off at 90-99). It is suppressed when the previous transition was rare. The simpler GO & prev_reward==1 & model_act==2 has recall ~1.0 but precision 0.42; adding ep_trial>=50 gives F1 0.81 and the full predicate gives dev F1 0.91. Magnitude rises with a stronger a2 preference (more negative choice logit) and, from the examples, across runs of consecutive rewarded a2 trials. The episode-time dependence is odd and may track an internal clock or accumulated evidence. The predicate uses only observed history plus the agent own upcoming choice.

issues: All factual claims checked out on dev. The feature fires only at GO (54546 of 54546 active steps). It fires 57 times with prev_reward==0 against 54489 with prev_reward==1. It fires 15 times for action a1 against 54531 for a2. It never fires at trials 0-39. 89.9% of the activation mass is in the most negative choice-logit bin. Rate is 0.005 after a rare transition versus 0.062 after a common one. Test scores reproduce: P 0.861, R 0.959, F1 0.907, mass recall 0.992.

False positives cluster at the two episode-time cut-offs. Precision is 0.68 at ep_trial 45-49 and 0.52 at 90-94, against 0.93-0.96 at 55-89. This looks like a gradual onset and offset in episode time, not a separate class of counterexamples. Tightening the cut-offs does not help (42-93 gives F1 0.901).

Misses are scattered, low-activation residue: 0.8% of the activation mass on test. A few strong activations after a rare-rewarded a2 trial are the main exception, and they are rare (B & prev_common==0 has precision 0.07).

Minor overclaim in the label: 'choosing a2 after a rewarded common trial' hides the fact that the previous trial was effectively always a2 reaching S2. Only 19 predicted steps have prev_action==1, so the feature is really 'staying on a2 after a2 to S2 was rewarded'. A2 preference is also confounded with good==S2: 80% of recall falls there, with precision 0.66 when good==S1, though n is small.
Small gain only: adding choice < -6 gives test F1 0.913 against 0.907. The choice logit is the agent's own upcoming preference, so no future variables are needed.
